t: Minimum Valid Strings to Form Target: Prefix Reachability + DP
o: A piece is any prefix of any word; we must tile `target` with the fewest such pieces. From each cut position i, the usable piece lengths are exactly the L such that target[i:i+L] equals a prefix of some word. Example 2 shows a single word supplying pieces repeatedly. With Σ|word| ≤ 1e5 and |target| ≤ 5e3, we can afford to precompute, for every start i, the maximum matchable length f[i], then run a linear DP dp[i] = 1 + min dp[i−L].
k: All valid pieces are prefixes of words, so from position i the reachable next cuts are i+1 … i+f[i] where f[i] is the longest target-run matching a word prefix.
f[i] for all i comes from walking a trie of the words along target, or from rolling-hash membership of word-prefix hashes.
dp[i+L] = min(dp[i+L], dp[i]+1) over L ≤ f[i] gives the answer; unreachable dp[n] means −1.

a.n: Approach 1: Trie of Words + Interval DP
a.i: Insert every word into a trie. For each start i, follow target characters down the trie until a mismatch; the depth reached is f[i]. This directly enumerates all prefixes of all words that occur at i in O(|target| · maxmatch) total, well within limits.
s: Build a trie containing all words.
For each i in target, walk the trie to compute f[i] = longest prefix match starting at i.
DP over cut positions: dp[0]=0; for each i with dp[i] finite, relax dp[i+L] = min(dp[i+L], dp[i]+1) for 1 ≤ L ≤ f[i].
a.t: O(Σ|word| + |target| · maxMatch) — trie build is linear in total word length; each start walks at most f[i] steps
a.sp: O(Σ|word| · 26) for the trie (array-based), plus O(|target|) DP

a.n: Approach 2: Rolling Hash of Word Prefixes
a.i: Instead of a trie, hash every prefix of every word into a set. For each start i, extend a running hash of target[i:i+L] while it is in the set; that yields the same f[i] array without trie memory. With a 61-bit modulus (or a double hash) collisions are negligible.
s: Compute the hash of every prefix of every word; store in a hash set.
For each i, extend L while hash(target[i:i+L]) is in the set, recording f[i].
Run the same cut-position DP as Approach 1.
a.t: O(Σ|word| + |target| · maxMatch) — hashing each word prefix once, then per-start extension

w: In an interview, lead with the trie version — it is deterministic and easy to explain; mention hashing/Aho–Corasick as the scalability upgrade (Aho–Corasick computes all f[i] in O(|target| + Σ|word|)). Pitfalls: a piece may be *any* prefix length, not just whole words; dp must consider all L ≤ f[i], not only the maximum; remember the −1 case when position 0 cannot start any word. Follow-up: report the actual pieces (keep parent pointers in the DP).
